chiamaka.quote: My soul knew that man from the very first day we had a conversation.
paragraphs: It was a sunny Sunday morning 😂. I had previously felt the nudge to actively participate in Youth Fellowship, so I was very involved in the service that day.
I was slated to take announcements and decided to add my usual touch and spunk to them—anything that could add life to the every-Sunday routine. And so I did.
While I was taking the announcements, I saw a young, radiant face smiling at me—not the usual look to spot in my local church at the time. He stood out quite easily.
“Why is this guy smiling at me?” I thought to myself while continuing with the announcement I was giving.
Once the service was over, the youths, as announced, were urged to wait at the side of the church for a brief meeting.

Well… well… Guess who came to stand by me at the side of the church? Exactly: that radiant face. He introduced himself, asked for my name, complimented my session, and even asked if I was a pastor’s kid (he was one).
I wondered aloud who had invited him, and he said nobody. I found him confusing initially, so he was getting a lot of side-eye from me.

The church meeting was over, and we stepped out of the building together to continue our small talk. Even though I had never seen this face before, standing under the hot sun in my black turban, black turtleneck, black long skirt and jacket (with no jewellery—just a wristwatch), I felt like I knew him. My soul knew that man from our very first conversation. He just felt familiar to me.

While he was still talking to me, my mum walked past and gave me “the look” to wrap it up. 😂 Knowing it would end with him asking for my number at last, I hurriedly gave it to him to fast-forward the conversation. This was our first meeting.
Many weeks passed… and Bambam remained unread in my DMs. He texted on the Sunday we met and later responded to my WhatsApp status, but I left his messages unread.

Then, on Wednesday, May 22, 2024, I was coming home from a friend’s store right along my street when I saw a guy walking on the opposite side of the small street in boyfriend jeans, a black shirt, a black beanie, and with a bounce to his steps.
No man had ever looked that fine! 😂 It was as if my eyes had suddenly opened and I felt his handsomeness from across the street.

We spoke casually. He had arrived in time for a youth meeting that day but found the gates locked. He asked me a few questions about it that I can’t fully recall, because right then I decided to pull him from the deep sea of unread messages onto land. He looked sooo fine to me! 😁
Ladies and gentle readers, that day—the 22nd of May 2024—we began talking and never stopped.

A month and a week later, he proposed on a call (because Bambam doesn’t believe in the “girlfriend” thing). It was an unofficial proposal that began our relationship as official best friends together.
Bambam witnessed many of my milestones from then on, and I did the same for him. We bonded over the concepts of Kingdom and Purpose and decided to keep learning and growing together.

We may have faced many hurdles in between, but our story is proof that God literally writes the best love stories. Now here we are: me and Bambam, my best friend. God has kept us, strengthened us, and grown the roots of our conviction for each other.
All that’s left to say is: Thank you, Lord. I love you, Father, and I’m grateful for my Bambam! 😊
I look forward to doing life and fulfilling our Kingdom assignments alongside you.

No matter how hard life gets, having you to make me laugh along the way definitely helps. Having the melodies and rhythms of your sound eases my heart, even during difficult moments. And having your protective side always ready to defend me has been such a charming experience.
A lifetime of your rich love fills my heart with excitement as I anticipate our journey officially beginning!

benny.quote: I knew it like I knew my God-given assignment on earth: this was the woman I would do life and purpose with.
paragraphs: On March 22, 2024, I had just moved from Bayelsa State to Rivers State. I left everything I was building, left my house, and gave away my pots, gas, and most of my belongings to move in with my grandparents. It felt like my life was falling apart, but I knew God had told me to leave.
It was my second time attending that local church. April 21 was Youth Sunday. I wasn’t very comfortable because there seemed to be more older people and children than young people.

It was time for announcements, and this fair young lady came up with an energy that changed the atmosphere of the entire auditorium. The children responded with shouts. Before I knew it, I was smiling at her; I was pleased.
After the service, we had a general youth meeting and I joined in. She came and sat beside me, so of course I engaged her in a conversation. 😁

“Hi, you did really well up there. You carried the whole church like you’ve been doing it all your life. Are you the pastor’s child?” I asked. With a mild smile, she responded, “No, I’m not. I just love to put in my best whenever I get the chance.”
We exchanged names and contact details before we left the gate that day.
This girl kept snubbing me, mehn! 😂 I texted her, responded to her status, and showed interest, but the best she would do was react to my messages.

Fast-forward to May 22, 2024. She texted me that evening after we saw each other on the road by the church. We were supposed to have a youth meeting that day, but I came out to find the gate locked. I went home after our brief chat. I even got her to go to the youth meeting I hadn’t attended (so she said 😂).

Since then, we’ve had a closely knit friendship. She was the first friend I made after moving. I was still healing from the total heartbreak of ending a relationship God disapproved of. I cried for hours every day and wasn’t thinking about another relationship, but this lovely lady always had questions to ask and faith-based conversations to start.
Before long, I started recalling the prophecies that had gone ahead of me about a fair, tall lady, dreams I was having, and coincidences I honestly couldn’t explain.
I knew it, as surely as I knew my God-given assignment on earth: this was the woman I would do life and purpose with.
Side note: we were 20 and 21 at the time. 😂

On June 29, 2024, a few minutes after 2 a.m., while we were on a video call, I asked Chi to marry me. We had just prayed about an issue that bothered us both. I was in tears when it was confirmed to me again that this was it for me. I popped the question, she said yes, and that’s when our relationship officially began.
It was easier for me to go the “marry me” route because I already knew she had her own convictions, and I’ve never really liked the idea of having a girlfriend. Things with us happened so fast. 😂
Since then, we’ve been learning, working through misunderstandings, forgiving, and growing together.
We moved to CCI in September 2025. Chiamaka went a month before me because I was zonal admin at our church and needed to resign and hand over properly.

On Valentine’s Day, February 14, 2026, I proposed to the absolute love of my life in church, with more than 3,000 young people present at our annual Young and Free Conference. That’s a whole different story altogether.
Today, I’m writing as the soon-to-be husband of this priceless pearl—the woman I would spend everything I have to purchase a field just to lay hold of.
She is proof of God’s mercy and intentionality toward me, and the woman God has used to help me grow into a man more quickly than I would have expected.
Here’s to the beginning of a lifetime and a day extra of loving and serving one of God’s most lovely daughters.
Oh Chim! 🤧
This is love ohh, believe me, it is!
